title: Use of variables in formula
competency: Use variables to describe numbers and find the value of a formula.

keywords.def: A letter or symbol that stands for an unknown number, such as x, y or n.
Put a number in place of a variable, then work out the answer.

en.text: A variable is a letter that stands for an unknown number. "Twice a number" is 2x. "Two more than a number" is y + 2. "Half a number" is n/2. If you are 13 now, after x years you will be 13 + x.

screens.title: Chala's age
screens.ask: Chala is 13 years old now. How old will he be after x years?
screens.after: After x more years, add x: 13 + x. The letter x stands for a number we do not know yet.

screens.title: Unit 3 Linear equations
paras: In this unit you learn why variables are important.
You use variables to solve linear equations.

screens.title: Definition 3.1
paras: A variable is any letter or symbol that represents an unknown number or value.
Examples: x, y, z, n, m.
In x + 2, x is a variable.

screens.title: Describing with variables
screens.ask: Tap each phrase to see it written with a variable.
items: m − 2: take 2 away from the number.
The product of a number and 10
Product of ten and the sum of two numbers
10(x + y): add the two numbers first, then multiply by 10.

screens.title: Chala's age
screens.note: Chala is 13 now. Move x. One expression works for every number of years.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A letter or symbol that stands for an unknown number, such as x, y or n.

screens.text: Find the variables: tap every letter that stands for a number.
screens.why:
x, y and a are letters, so they are variables.
23, 4, 0.5 and 3/4 are fixed numbers.
A fraction or a decimal is still a fixed number.
The variables are x, y and a.
screens.clue: A variable is a letter, not a number.

screens.text: Write in symbols: "five less than a number".
screens.why:
Let the number be x.
"Five less than" means take 5 away from it.
So we write x − 5.
5 − x is wrong: it takes the number away from 5.
screens.clue: Start with the number, then take 5 away.

screens.text: Write as an expression: start with x, add 8, then double the result.
screens.why:
Start with x.
Add 8: x + 8.
Double the whole result, so use a bracket: 2(x + 8).
2x + 8 doubles only x, not the 8.
screens.clue: Double the WHOLE result, so use a bracket.

screens.ask: Write an expression for your age: you are 13 now. y years ago you were ___ years old.
screens.why:
"Ago" means in the past, so you were younger.
Younger means subtract the years.
So you were 13 − y years old.
Check: 2 years ago you were 13 − 2 = 11.
screens.clue: Were you older or younger then?

screens.text: Write an expression: Hiwot has x birr. Chala has 5 birr more than twice Hiwot's money. How much do they have together?
screens.why:
Twice Hiwot's money is 2x.
5 birr more: Chala has 2x + 5.
Together: x + (2x + 5).
Collect the x terms: x + 2x = 3x.
They have 3x + 5 birr.
2x + 5 is only Chala's money.
screens.clue: First write Chala's money. Then add Hiwot's x.

ideas.name: Finding the value of a formula

en.text: To find y in y = 2x + 3, put the value of x in place of x. Multiply first, then add. When x = 5, y = 2(5) + 3 = 10 + 3 = 13.

screens.title: Guess y
screens.ask: y = 2x + 3. If x = 1, what is y?
screens.after: Put 1 in place of x: y = 2(1) + 3 = 2 + 3 = 5.

screens.title: Using a formula
paras: A relation like y = 2x + 3 tells how y depends on x.
Put the number in place of x. Then multiply before you add.

screens.title: Try y = 2x + 3
screens.note: Move x. Multiply by 2 first, then add 3. Try x = −4: y = −5.

screens.title: y = 2x + 3 when x = −4
steps: Put −4 in place of x: y = 2(−4) + 3.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Put a number in place of a variable, then work out the answer.

screens.why:
Put 5 in place of x: y = 2(5) + 3.
Multiply first: 2 × 5 = 10.
Then add: 10 + 3 = 13.
So y = 13.

screens.ask: Use the perimeter formula P = 2x + 2y. If x = 4 cm and y = 7 cm, P = ___ cm
Substitute a fraction into y = 2x + 3. When x = 2/3, y = ___
screens.clue: Write 3 as a fraction with denominator 3.

screens.why:
Put −4 in place of x: y = 2(−4) + 3.
2 × (−4) = −8 (different signs give −).
−8 + 3 = −5.
So y = −5.
screens.clue: A positive times a negative is negative.

screens.ask: Work backwards: y = 3x − 5. For which value of x is y = 10? x = ___
screens.why:
We need 3x − 5 = 10.
Add 5 to both sides: 3x = 15.
Divide both sides by 3: x = 5.
Check: 3(5) − 5 = 15 − 5 = 10.
screens.clue: Try x = 4, 5, 6 and see which gives 10.

math.integer-signs.name: Signs when multiplying and adding integers

screens.title: Integer signs
steps: Adding different signs: −5 + 3 = −2 (take 3 from 5, keep the sign of 5).

screens.why:
Both numbers are negative: the signs are the same.
Same signs give a positive answer.
3 × 4 = 12.
So (−3) × (−4) = 12. (−12 would need different signs.)
screens.clue: Are the signs the same or different?

items.text: Identify the variables in the expression 2y + b.
items.why:
2 is a fixed number.
y and b are letters.
Letters stand for unknown numbers.
So the variables are y and b.

items.text: Identify the variables in the expression x/2 − p.
items.why:
x/2 means x divided by 2.
The 2 is a fixed number, not a variable.
The letters are x and p.
So the variables are x and p.

items.text: Write in symbols: four times a number.
items.why:
Let the number be x.
"Times" means multiply: 4 × x.
We write 4 × x as 4x.
x + 4 would mean "four more than".

items.text: Write in symbols: one third of a number.
items.why:
Let the number be x.
"One third of" means divide by 3.
x ÷ 3 = x/3.
3/x would be 3 divided by the number.

items.text: Write in symbols: ten more than twice a number.
items.why:
Twice the number is 2x.
Ten more means add 10.
So it is 2x + 10.
2(x + 10) adds 10 before doubling: different.

items.text: Write in symbols: six less than twice a number.
items.why:
Twice the number is 2x.
Six less means take away 6.
So it is 2x − 6.
6 − 2x takes 2x away from 6: wrong order.

opts: Three more than four times a number
Four more than three times a number
items.ans: Three more than four times a number
items.why:
4x means four times a number.
3 + 4x adds 3 to it.
So it is three more than four times a number.
"Four more than three times" would be 3x + 4.

items.ask: Substitute into y = 2x + 3. When x = 1, y = ___
items.why:
Put 1 in place of x: y = 2(1) + 3.
2 × 1 = 2.
2 + 3 = 5.
So y = 5.

items.ask: Substitute a negative number into y = 2x + 3. When x = −4, y = ___
items.clue: A positive times a negative is negative.

items.ask: Substitute a fraction into y = 2x + 3. When x = 2/3, y = ___

test.text: Write in symbols: which expression means "two more than a number"?
test.why:
Let the number be y.
"More than" means add.
Two more than y is y + 2.
2y means two times y, not two more.

test.text: Variables: which one of these is a variable?
test.why:
A variable is a letter that stands for a number.
n is a letter.
7, 0.5 and 3/4 are fixed numbers.
So n is the variable.

test.text: Write an expression: Abel has x birr. Bethel has 3 birr less than Abel. How much do they have together?
test.why:
Bethel has 3 less than x: x − 3.
Together: x + (x − 3).
x + x = 2x.
They have 2x − 3 birr.
